data.narrative: Transformed the marketplace architecture into 5 end-to-end testable vertical slices with rigorous anti-scope boundaries and non-technical acceptance criteria. When faced with high-stakes investor payment pressure, resisted monolithic scope inflation and engineered a decoupled spike strategy (Slice 1.5) that guaranteed 100% demo uptime while proving live Stripe transactions.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted comprehensive scope and boundary definitions, explicitly itemizing 9 adjacent features in anti-scope to eliminate ambiguity before implementation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Itemized explicit exclusions across auth, payments, notifications, search, cancellations, reviews, and admin portals in artifacts/slices-module-04.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Designed strict cumulative slice dependencies ensuring infrastructure and state carry forward logically from slice to slice.
dimension_scores.evidence: Mapped ordered progression: Slice 1 (core booking) -> Slice 2 (auth/dashboard) -> Slice 3 (provider publishing) -> Slice 4 (payment escrow) -> Slice 5 (refunds/reviews).

dimension_scores.observation: Protected the thin first slice by recognizing payment processing as an external integration risk that should not be coupled to core UX validation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Preserved Slice 1 focus on core booking demand, isolating payment execution into standalone Slice 1.5 to protect Friday investor demo.

dimension_scores.observation: Specified crisp, non-technical acceptance criteria that enable anyone to verify slices through the UI without inspecting code or databases.
dimension_scores.evidence: Provided 5-step concrete user walkthroughs for each slice in artifacts/slices-module-04.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Responded rapidly to stakeholder scope pressure with a mature tradeoff analysis and decoupled solution rather than passive capitulation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Engineered Slice 1.5 Standalone Payment Spike and drafted professional PM communication with clear options and meeting narratives in progress/decomposition/module-04/fix-slice-plan.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Ensured seamless integration by defining shared interface contracts (IPaymentGateway) and planning the synthesis of Slice 1 and 1.5 into Slice 4.
dimension_scores.evidence: Specified IPaymentGateway abstraction and escrow state machine that bridges standalone payment spike into full booking checkout in Slice 4.

strengths: Demonstrated exceptional scoping discipline by authoring comprehensive, unambiguous anti-scope boundaries that protect sprint execution.
Exhibited tech lead maturity by rejecting scope capitulation under investor pressure and negotiating a high-reliability decoupled demo alternative.
data.recommendation: Carry these slice boundaries into Module 05 by decomposing Slice 1 and Slice 2 into developer-ready task specifications with strict interface contracts and anti-scope.

public_evidence.student_action: Authored 5 ordered vertical slice definitions and adapted plan with Slice 1.5 Standalone Payment Spike under stakeholder pressure.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Vertical slice planning, anti-scope enforcement, IPaymentGateway contract stubbing, and stakeholder tradeoff negotiation.
public_evidence.ability: Vertical slicing, scope management, and stakeholder tradeoff communication under delivery pressure.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves the candidate builds iteratively in thin end-to-end threads, prevents scope creep with rigorous anti-scope, and handles executive pressure with constructive engineering options.

Formulated 9 explicit exclusions per slice preventing scope creep.
Negotiated decoupled Slice 1.5 payment spike for investor demo without compromising core slice timeline.
